idiom_name: struct of visit_* function pointers plus an accept function pointer per node (hand-built vtable)
implementation_notes: C has no virtual dispatch and no overloading, so both halves of the pattern are built by hand: the visitor is a struct of function pointers - one member per node type - and each node type carries an accept function pointer that calls the matching member, passing the node and the visitor. The visitor struct is conventionally embedded as the first member of a concrete visitor struct so callbacks can recover their state with a single cast, the same convention GObject uses for class-struct virtual methods. Keep the traversal policy explicit: either the visitor exposes a walk callback, or the caller walks the tree and calls accept at every node. C's simpler local alternative is a tagged union plus a switch over the tag (the dispatch-table record of this catalog), so the full structure is worth building only when several node kinds and several operations must stay independently replaceable - a plugin ABI whose contract is a table of callbacks, for instance.
pitfalls: The visitor struct must be initialised before the first accept call; C has no constructors, so a missed member is a null function pointer that traps only when that node type is reached.
Callbacks receive the visitor explicitly as their first argument (C passes no implicit self); forgetting it compiles until the callback needs visitor state.
Casting the visitor's void * back to the concrete visitor struct is unchecked - the visitor struct must be the first member, or the cast silently reinterprets memory.
Node lifetime is manual: a visitor that stores node pointers beyond the traversal holds dangling pointers unless the structure guarantees they outlive the operation.
